person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: the ReaxFF reactive force field - a classical interatomic potential that describes bond breaking and forming through a bond-order formalism, without explicit quantum mechanics
span.quote: Alternatively, empirical interatomic potentials that are based on classical principles require significantly fewer computational resources, which enables simulations to better describe dynamic processes over longer timeframes and on larger scales. Such methods, however, typically require a predefined connectivity between atoms, precluding simulations that involve reactive events. The ReaxFF method was developed to help bridge this gap. Approaching the gap from the classical side, ReaxFF casts the empirical interatomic potential within a bond-order formalism, thus implicitly describing chemical bonding without expensive QM calculations.

span.label: how a single functional form can cover reactive chemistry across phases, and what the resulting parameter sets can and cannot be combined with
span.quote: Although a ReaxFF description exists for these elements, one cannot simply use these parameter sets in any combination and expect to obtain satisfactory transferability. As shown in Figure 2, there are currently two major groupings (i.e., the ReaxFF branches) of parameter sets that are intra-transferable with one another: (1) the combustion branch and (2) the aqueous branch.

span.label: a review of ReaxFF's development, applications and directions - including an explicit account of why its parameter sets fall into two mutually untransferable branches
span.quote: Although a ReaxFF description exists for these elements, one cannot simply use these parameter sets in any combination and expect to obtain satisfactory transferability. As shown in Figure 2, there are currently two major groupings (i.e., the ReaxFF branches) of parameter sets that are intra-transferable with one another: (1) the combustion branch and (2) the aqueous branch.

span.label: method
span.quote: Alternatively, empirical interatomic potentials that are based on classical principles require significantly fewer computational resources, which enables simulations to better describe dynamic processes over longer timeframes and on larger scales. Such methods, however, typically require a predefined connectivity between atoms, precluding simulations that involve reactive events. The ReaxFF method was developed to help bridge this gap. Approaching the gap from the classical side, ReaxFF casts the empirical interatomic potential within a bond-order formalism, thus implicitly describing chemical bonding without expensive QM calculations.

span.label: a method whose defining choice is to give an element ONE description everywhere, and whose parameter sets have consequently forked into two populations that cannot be mixed
span.quote: In order to explain the existence of branches within a common functional form, we must consider that ReaxFF does not employ atom typing in contrast to popular non-reactive force-fields like strategies, AMBER25 and CHARMM.26 For example, there is only one oxygen type in ReaxFF regardless of the chemical environment in which the oxygen atom finds itself. This is quite helpful because it allows atoms to migrate seamlessly between phases during a simulation. At the same time, however, this results in a significantly more complex force-field development process.

span.label: a review of the bond-order formalism and of the published parameterisations, organised by development branch and by the training sets each was fitted or validated against
span.term: a review of the bond-order formalism and of the published parameterisations, organised by development branch and by the training sets each was fitted or validated against
span.quote: The 2008-C/H/O parameter set was trained against the entire 2001-C/H training set, while the 2010 and 2011 Si/O/H parameterisations (Fogarty et al.15 on the ‘aqueous branch’ and Neyts et al.16 on the ‘combustion branch’) were validated against the full 2003-Si/O/H training set.

span.label: ReaxFF's defining choice is that an element has ONE description regardless of environment, which is what lets an atom migrate between phases mid-simulation. The cost is that a parameter set cannot be specialised without changing the shared atom-level parameters - so the specialisation became a BRANCH instead of a TYPE. REFUSING TO SPLIT THE VOCABULARY SPLIT THE PARAMETER SETS
span.quote: In order to explain the existence of branches within a common functional form, we must consider that ReaxFF does not employ atom typing in contrast to popular non-reactive force-fields like strategies, AMBER25 and CHARMM.26 For example, there is only one oxygen type in ReaxFF regardless of the chemical environment in which the oxygen atom finds itself. This is quite helpful because it allows atoms to migrate seamlessly between phases during a simulation. At the same time, however, this results in a significantly more complex force-field development process.

span.label: liquid water was not a development aim for the 2008 combustion field because every intended application was above the boiling point. That is a defensible scope decision at the time and it is why the field fails on liquid water in 2009, and why a second branch had to exist
span.term: the scope decision that became a failure
span.quote: The lack of transferability between branches is evident in the performance of the 2008-C/H/O combustion force-field,2 which accurately describes water as a gas-phase molecule yet fails to describe water as a liquid. During development at that time, describing liquid water was not a particular aim for ReaxFF. Since all intended applications were at temperatures well above the water boiling point, this was not a major development concern.

span.label: parameter sets on the same branch combine by fitting only the bond and angular terms between the newly combined elements; across branches it takes extensive refitting, and combustion-to-aqueous is the easier direction. THE ASYMMETRY IS A FACT ABOUT THE FITTING HISTORY, not about the chemistry
span.term: a fork that cannot be undone cheaply
span.quote: Parameter sets on the same development branch can be directly combined, where the required force-field fitting consists only of parameterising bond and angular terms between the newly combined elements. Transferring parameters between branches, however, requires more extensive refitting.

span.label: several independent branches - B/N/H, Ni/C/H - began as non-transferable descriptions and were later merged into combustion or aqueous through extensive refitting. A vocabulary reconciled by redoing the work rather than by declaring the terms equivalent
span.term: branches merge by refitting, not by agreement
span.quote: Typically these sets began as non-transferable ReaxFF descriptions constituting independent development branches, but many have later been merged, through extensive refitting, with the combustion (C/B/N/H/O)34 or aqueous branches (Ni/C/H/O).

span.label: QM structure and energy data train the empirical field, which then runs at scales orders of magnitude beyond what QM can reach. The potential is a compression of the quantum calculation, and every branch is a different compression of a different part of it
span.term: accuracy traded for scale, on purpose
span.quote: To alleviate this issue, QM structure and energy data are used to train empirical force fields that require significantly fewer computational resources, thereby enabling simulations to better describe including reactive dynamic processes. Such empirical methods, force-field (ReaxFF),1 trade accuracy for lower computational expense, making it possible to reach simulation scales that are orders of magnitude beyond what is tractable for QM.
